name: server/mzizi-data
title: mzizi-data
summary: The transport trait, error type and Worker socket every Mzizi database client shares; the data layer above them (a local, edge and cloud fetch cascade, sync reconciliation, tombstones, staleness, local-first writes that roll back); and the client write path (outbox, request-id mutations, status polling, read-your-own-writes). Nothing database-specific, and no UI. The server harness is the separate mzizi-harness crate. Publishes with the next registry release to main.

guarantees.statement: A fresh local record answers a read alone, without asking the edge or the cloud.
A stale local record keeps the read going to the edge and then the cloud; the newest fresh record wins. If none is fresh, the newest stale record is returned with stale set and the failures listed.
A write-back never replaces a record that sorts higher; each write re-reads its target first.
A cloud miss is Ok(None), even when local or edge failed on the way; the read is an error only when no tier answered.
A failed write restores every tier it attempted, including the one that failed, to its own previous record, exactly; a tier with none is deleted.
A pending record never wins reconciliation while a confirmed record exists, so a rejected write cannot win after recovery.
A newer tombstone wins and propagates; an older live copy cannot bring the record back.
A tier is in sync only when the whole record matches the winner, updated_at included.
A record stamped after the clock's now is reported stale.
The futures a Cascade returns are Send when its layers and clock are Send; the crate adds no Send bound of its own.
A write is in the outbox before the call returns and before anything is sent; a crash after that cannot lose it.
A mutation sent twice with the same request id is applied by the server once.
Queued writes flush in creation order and stop at the first failure to reach the server; the server receives them in that order.
A stale base_version is refused as a conflict, and the optimistic change is reverted to the last confirmed record.
A write the server refuses at submit is reverted and reports its reason.
A write not settled within the timeout becomes Unknown, is checked again on restart, and is never sent again.
A read applies this client's unconfirmed writes on top of the confirmed record.
A read answers from the first tier with a fresh record; a miss goes on to the next tier; when every tier fails the read is an error that names each tier.
An on_settled callback fires once, when the write is applied or refused.
A request id is a UUIDv7 carrying its creation time in milliseconds.
Read timestamps format as RFC 3339 in UTC, with milliseconds.

refusals.input: An apply or delete at a key whose newest version is u64::MAX.
refusals.reason: The next version cannot be represented, so the write is refused rather than wrapped or saturated. Nothing is written.

refusals.input: A reconcile that would write a tier it could not read.
refusals.reason: The tier's newer data, if any, would be lost, so the tier is skipped and reported.

refusals.input: A collection or document id that is empty or contains '/'.
refusals.reason: The key would be ambiguous, so the write is refused and nothing is queued.

harness.secrets: mzizi-data emits no events. It holds no state a harness could see.

gaps: The Postgres and SQLite clients (mzizi-postgres, mzizi-sqlite) do not exist yet; nothing is stubbed.
workers::SocketIo is compiled only for wasm32 with the workers feature, so its contract is held by a type check and clippy for wasm32-unknown-unknown, not by a native test.
No storage adapter for the local (IndexedDB, SQLite), edge (D1, KV) or cloud (Supabase) tiers exists yet. The cascade is tested only over in-memory tiers.
No background timer: the host schedules reconcile.
Tombstones are retained; there is no garbage collection.
There is no key enumeration, so a full sync is not provided.
The data layer is not wired into any app. The WASM payload budget (owner decision 6.2) is still open and gates that.
No durable outbox adapter ships: only MemoryOutbox, which does not survive a page reload. IndexedDB (browser) and SQLite (native) are later adapters.
The write path is tested over a fake server and in-memory tiers only; no HTTP transport adapter exists.
The server's changes to documents the client did not write reach it only through the edge or cloud tier; there is no push or SSE, by design.
No storage adapter for the local, edge or cloud tiers exists yet beyond the reference MemoryLayer.
The settled-write status table is kept in memory for the session and is not pruned.
The 5-second apply target is a draft target to be confirmed, not a measured fact.
